entry.title: Will Bangladesh garment workers' lives ever improve? | DW News

media:group.media:title: Will Bangladesh garment workers' lives ever improve? | DW News
media:group.media:description:
Textile workers in Bangladesh are on strike for higher wages. Their protests have closed factories in many areas, and sporadic violence has erupted. It's not the first time workers have demanded better wages and working conditions in the world's second largest garment exporter. Will these protests finally deliver the reforms they need? Biresh Banerjee speaks with Zyma Islam of Bangladesh's The Daily Star outlet.

entry.title: Why Russia and China aren't really best friends | DW News

media:group.media:title: Why Russia and China aren't really best friends | DW News
media:group.media:description:
Does Russia have a China problem? As Western sanctions have pushed Moscow closer to Beijing, Russia has become increasingly dependent on China for trade, technology, consumer goods, and key components supporting its war effort in Ukraine. Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping have repeatedly highlighted their strategic partnership, which Russia and China describe as having ‘no limits.’ But behind the headlines lies a growing imbalance. Following the Trans-Siberian Railway to Russia’s Far East, we explore the complicated history, border tensions, security concerns, and economic ties shaping one of the world’s most important geopolitical relationships. Featuring expert analysis from Alexander Gabuev, Eva Seiwert, Lydia Wachs, and Sebastian Hoppe on the future of the Russia-China partnership, Putin and Xi Jinping, sanctions, trade, security, Russia’s dependence on China, the war in Ukraine, and the growing rivalry between great powers in Eurasia.

01:14 How secure is Russia’s 4,000-kilometer border with China?
